title: Renewal Preflight Risk Canvas & Exec Activation
content:
Purpose
This is a pragmatic, lightweight runbook to triage renewals before QBRs and to decide when to ring the executive bell. Primary user: CSMs + AE for early-warning capture; CS Lead for escalation.

Context / why this exists
We keep seeing two failure modes: 1) slow detection — issues only surface at the QBR when it's late to act; 2) noisy escalations — exec time is used for cases we could resolve with targeted tactical plays. This canvas gives a structured, repeatable preflight to: quantify risk, pick the right mitigation, and only escalate when high-impact, time-sensitive intervention is required.

1) HEAT score (Health / Engagement / Technical debt / Timeline)
Scoring: 0–25 (green), 26–55 (amber), 56–100 (crimson). Calculate once per week in the week leading up to contract renewal.
- Health (0–25): product usage vs expected for tier. Signal sources: API tokens, model calls/day, embeddings lookups.
- Engagement (0–25): number of active seats, QBR attendance, product feedback frequency.
- Technical debt (0–25): outstanding bugs blocking core flows, severity, open Sev1/2s.
- Timeline (0–25): time until renewal and runway for fixes (shorter time => higher score).
Notes: add +10 if legal/contract issues in flight; add +15 if competitive RFP is known.

Example scoring guidance (cheat-sheet)
- 60+ = CRIMSON: immediate escalation recommended.
- 40–59 = AMBER: surge play and 72h cadence; escalate only if AE or CSM says exec attention warranted.
- <40 = GREEN: monitor + standard QBR prep.

2) Intake checklist (preflight, ~30–60 minutes)
- Quick health pull: last 30 days usage vs baseline (note % delta).
- Support intake: count of ongoing incidents in the last 90 days.
- Product blockers: are there open PRs or fixes with uncertain ETA? list PR numbers.
- Commercial noise: pricing disputes, MSA draft issues, procurement delays.
- Competitive signals: RFPs, trials by competitors, reps report.
- Voice of customer: key quotes from NPS/CSAT, most recent QBR notes.
- Executive sponsor check: confirmed or missing? If missing, +5 to Timeline subscore.

3) Rapid mitigation plays (owner, goal, timebox)
- Tactical SOW/discount offer (AE + CS): goal = remove commercial blocker; timebox 48–72h.
- Technical hotfix sprint (SE + Eng): triage top-3 defects, hot patch, temporary workaround. 72h sprint.
- Adoption blitz (CS Ops): targeted onboarding sessions, office hours, playbook + quick wins template; 2 weeks.
- Usage credit / sandbox expansion (Finance + AE): buy runway for product fixes; immediate negotiation.
- Feature toggle fallback (Eng + Product): reduce product friction by toggling new/experimental infra. 24–48h.

4) Exec escalation rubric (when to ping CS Lead / CRO / CTO)
Trigger a formal exec brief (15–30 minute pre-brief + 60-minute run) when ANY of the following are true:
- HEAT >= 70 (crimson) OR
- Contract value >= $250k ARR and HEAT >= 50 OR
- Legal/Compliance blocker that prevents production use OR
- Competitive RFP where win probability is >30% loss and timeline < 60 days OR
- Customer has regulatory audit looming that requires private deployment.

Exec brief packing list (one-pager, max 2 pages)
- Topline risk score + how it moved in last 30 days.
- Critical blockers (3 bullets): who, what, ETA.
- Proposed plays and owner assignments (RACI).
- Ask from execs (e.g., commit engineering resource X hours this week, approve discount Y, contact customer C-level).
- Consequences if we do nothing (revenue at risk, reference loss, competitive exposure).

5) Surge choreography (fast-response operating rhythm)
- Hour 0–6: CSM/AE pre-brief. Confirm HEAT, attach logs, list top 3 asks.
- Hour 6–24: If playbook selected, owners notified, Jira epic created (tag: renewal-surge). Daily 9am stand for first 72h.
- 24–72h: Deliverables: hotfix plan or commercial offer; if ETA slips, escalate to CS Lead.
- 72h–14d: Adoption and operationalization (CS Ops + SE).

6) Communication templates (short and usable)
- Slack ping to #cs-saves (one-line): "CS SAVE: [Customer] HEAT=72, Renewal 36d — blocking bug in inference pipeline, need eng lead X for hotfix + AE support on commercial."
- Email to execs (subject): "Exec Brief Request: [Customer] renewal risk (ARR $X) — requested 30m pre-brief"
- Customer outreach sample: "We’ve prioritized a technical squad to address X and are proposing a short-term credit while we verify improvements. Can we align on a plan this week?"

7) Stakeholder map (template to fill out)
- Day-to-day contact: name, role, email, phone
- Exec sponsor: name, role, relationship strength (1–5)
- Procurement contact: name, expected approvals timeline
- Product owner / engineering counterpart: name, availability for validation
- External influencers (SI, reseller): name + leverage

8) QBR slide checklist (to walk into QBR with confidence)
- One slide: HEAT score + trend chart (last 90d)
- One slide: Top 3 wins since last QBR (metrics + concrete outcome)
- One slide: Top 3 blockers + recovery plan + owners + ETA
- One slide: Ask of the customer (time, resources, decisions)
- One slide: Proposed commercial options (if any) and impact analysis

9) Failures and postmortem triggers
- If we lose a contract that was flagged CRIMSON we require a 2-week postmortem and an exec readout.
- Postmortem artifacts: timeline, decisions made, why mitigation failed, and recommendations to prevent similar misses.

10) Quick tracking columns (for a lightweight sheet)
- customer_name, arr, renewal_date, heat_score, last_qbr_date, open_incidents_count, commercial_blocker_flag, exec_escalated_flag, current_play, play_owner, next_update_date
Notes: use these as CSV headers in a shared sheet; dashboard can pivot by team owner.

Open questions / TODOs
- Should we auto-add tickets with HEAT >= 60 to a dedicated SRE rotation? (ask SRE monthly)
- What discount authority thresholds should AE have for 72h saves? Current policy unclear around >20% discount.
- Hook up alerts to AlertManager for usage drops >30% week-over-week — engineering follow-up (see linked Confluence).

Appendix: quick sample case (anonymized)
- Customer: "NimbleRetail"; ARR $310k; renewal in 45d; HEAT 74 (Health 18, Engagement 20, Techdebt 24, Timeline 12).
- Problem: inference pipeline unstable under traffic; two Sev1 incidents last 30d; procurement waiting for mitigation plan.
- Play chosen: 72h hotfix + interim usage credit; exec notified due to ARR >250k and HEAT>70.
- Outcome: hotfix shipped 5 days later, procurement accepted 30-day extension + credit; renewal completed with a 6% concession.

Notes to self (CS playbook author)
- Keep this file short. Copy into Confluence as canonical runbook once we finalize discount thresholds.
- Add links to standardized email templates in the CS Ops drive.
- Follow up with product on an automated HEAT widget in the console.

End of document.
